text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- Bank Austria's employees committee might block the planned privatisation of the bank, after the City of Vienna's ruling coalition agreed to sell its stake. The City council expects to net 35 billion schillings from the sale.

- Both Social Democrat Transport and Science Caspar Einem, who is against Austria joining NATO, as well as Conservative Parliamentary President Heinrich Neisser, who is for, agree that a referendum should be held on the topic.

- The opposition parties started their boycott of all committee proceedings in an attempt to force a parliamentary inquiry into the affair around the 1989 murders of three Kurdish leaders by suspected Iranian killers.
- Women's Affairs Minister Barbara Prammer demands the time spent raising a child should be included into time accounted for in pension calculations.
- Ferdinand Lacina, chief executive of GiroCredit, will retire as a result of his bank's merger with Die Erste savings bank.

- Caspar Einem has extended the deadline for the licence for the third mobile phone network to July 2, in order to receive more offers. The only bidder Connect Austria is threatening to cancel its bid.
- Federal grid company Verbund sees good business opportunities in Germany, since electricity prices there are higher than in Austria.
- Oil and chemicals group OMV's pre-tax profits fell 11 percent to 910 million schillings in the first quarter of 1996.
- Petrol group Shell has cut 12 percent of its jobs in Austria and plans to continue its rationalisation.
- Austria's biggest brewer BBAG will take over 47 percent of Rumanian brewer S.C. Bere Craiova for 120 million schillings.
DIE PRESSE
- More Austrians than ever before want the country to join NATO. However a large majority also favours retaining neutrality at the same time.

- While Social Democrat Chancellor Viktor Klima says the government will not prepare any more austerity measures for the 1998/99 budgets, Conservative Vice-Chancellor Wolfgang Schuessel refuses to talk about tax raises.
- United Telecom Austria has started talks with British phone company Orange over a possible joint bid for the third mobile phone licence in Austria.
- Insurer s-Versicherung is vying for the exclusive rights to sell its contracts through Die Erste savings bank after the bank's merger with GiroCredit.
- Raiffeisen Zentralbank has opened up a subsidiary in Moscow, as the bank's earnings in eastern Europe are growing.
KURIER
- Savings banks are facing major reforms. The abolition of all holding companies would bring Die Erste savings bank under the control of Vienna council and would affect 20 other savings banks.
SALZBURGER NACHRICHTEN
- Regional hypo banks union chief Kurt Adelsburg wants the banks to have a joint strategic partner, which should participate through a capital increase.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- As earnings for Vienna's blue-chips are on the rise international funds are buying more of their stocks.
